identity.name: Anomalous Outbound RDP Egress — Lateral Movement (ms-rdp)
identity.summary: A workstation opens outbound RDP (ms-rdp / TCP 3389) to a host it never normally reaches, the App-ID + NGFW-traffic shape of interactive lateral movement.
identity.description: An endpoint that normally only RECEIVES RDP initiates OUTBOUND ms-rdp sessions — the X.224 Connection Request carries an mstshash cookie (the pivoting account) and an NLA/CredSSP negotiation. Cortex NGFW App-ID classifies the session as ms-rdp and the NDR/traffic analytics flag the anomalous outbound/lateral RDP. CortexSim drives rdp_egress (real TCP X.224 CR to an authorised sinkhole) — no credentials/CredSSP material ever leaves the simulator.

execution.framework_reference_id: T1572 / T1021.004 — CortexSim ssh_egress EAL plugin (outbound SSH-2.0 banner + KEXINIT to lab sinkhole)

prerequisites.description: Lab environment matching scenario SIM-NDR-007 requirements (NGFW logging outbound traffic from the lab subnet to XSIAM, TCP listener on 10.50.0.42:22).
NGFW forwards outbound traffic logs into XSIAM (panw_ngfw_traffic_raw / network_story carries app, src_ip, dst_ip, dst_port, session duration).

payload.code:
# Live outbound RDP X.224 Connection Request burst against the lab sinkhole, so
# the NGFW App-ID fingerprints ms-rdp egress (traffic-level EAL — real TCP, no
# credentials/CredSSP ever sent). Mirrors ssh_egress/ftp_egress.
cat > /tmp/rdp-egress-live.yml <<'YML'
campaign_id: CMP-NDR-013
name: "Outbound RDP egress (ms-rdp X.224 CR)"
target_allowlist:
  - "10.50.0.42:3389"
steps:
  - plugin: rdp_egress
    params:
      target_host: "10.50.0.42"
      target_port: 3389
      mstshash_cookie: "svc-rdp"
      requested_protocols: 2
      iterations: 5
      sleep_seconds: 10
YML
python3 -m core.eal_simulator.run_campaign --campaign /tmp/rdp-egress-live.yml || true

expected_artifacts.description: Outbound ms-rdp session from a workstation to TCP 3389 on an internal host.

iocs.context: Lab RDP sinkhole the egress targets (TEST/lab only).

biocs.name: NDR-013 Outbound RDP From a Non-Server Endpoint
biocs.description: A workstation-class host initiates an outbound RDP (ms-rdp / 3389) session — RDP from a host that normally only accepts it, consistent with interactive lateral movement.
biocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter app = "ms-rdp" or dst_port = 3389
| filter action = "allow"
| comp count() as rdp_sessions by src_ip, dst_ip, dst_port
| filter rdp_sessions >= 1

xql_queries.name: Outbound ms-rdp Egress on the NGFW Traffic Feed
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter app = "ms-rdp" or dst_port = 3389
| comp count() as sessions by src_ip, dst_ip
| sort desc sessions

xql_queries.name: RDP To an Internal Host Never Previously Contacted
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter dst_port = 3389 and app = "ms-rdp"
| comp count_distinct(dst_ip) as rdp_peers by src_ip
| filter rdp_peers >= 1

threat_scenarios.name: Outbound SSH Tunnel / C2 Setup Detection via NGFW EAL
threat_scenarios.description: Validate that NGFW App-ID + XSIAM Network Security Analytics detect outbound SSH with an atypical client banner and a repeated short-lived handshake burst from a non-admin endpoint.

threat_steps.objective: Outbound SSH App-ID and the atypical client banner are detected from NGFW telemetry.
preconditions: NGFW logging outbound traffic from the lab subnet to XSIAM.
steps: Run SIM-NDR-007 step-02 (live ssh_egress with atypical banner + KEXINIT).
Inspect Network Security Analytics / network_story for the source IP.
success_criteria: XQL `NGFW App-ID SSH outbound session from non-admin endpoint` returns >= 1 row.

threat_steps.objective: The handshake burst and banner anomaly stitch into a single tunnel/C2-setup incident.
success_criteria: BIOC `NGFW EAL repeated short-lived outbound SSH handshakes from single source` returns >= 1 row with handshake_count >= 4.
Correlation `CR-NDR-0006` raises a single SSH-tunnel/C2 incident for the source.

preventive_controls: Restrict outbound SSH at the NGFW to approved bastion/jump hosts and sanctioned destinations only.
Apply default-deny outbound policy and block ssh App-ID from workstation subnets.
Enforce SSH client allowlisting so only sanctioned clients/banners are permitted.
detection_engineering: Alert on ssh App-ID from non-admin endpoints toward non-corporate destinations.
Surface atypical/non-standard SSH client identification banners.
Correlate repeated short-lived SSH handshakes with the banner anomaly into one tunnel/C2-setup incident.
